text:
alex: quick ask — PM wants a \"Routing preview\" on the Roles page so tenant admins can see which model/region/priority a role would route traffic to. basically a simulation panel. useful or overkill?

maya: +1 from product. customers keep asking why certain calls hit dedicated vs hosted pools. preview would make rollouts less scary.

samir: main perf concern is computing a realistic preview without running live routing logic for every role. we can approximate with policy rules and recent capacity snapshots.

david: agree. also need to gate sensitive telemetry. the preview must not reveal exact IPs/hosts or internal pool ids to tenant admins. just abstracted labels (e.g., \"dedicated-us-west\").

alex: architecture question: do we add a new evaluation endpoint or reuse /entitlements/evaluate? current evaluate is sync and heavy.

samir: proposal: add /entitlements/preview that runs a fast-path evaluator — read-only, uses routing heuristics, sampling window for quotas, and respects privacy masks. returns a routing plan + quota impacts.

maya: example response we discussed in product sync:
```json
{
  "role_id": "rol_123",
  "routes": [
    {"priority": "low-cost", "model": "open-7b-q", "region": "us-west", "expected_qps%": "70%"},
    {"priority": "latency", "model": "redwood-13b", "region": "us-east", "expected_qps%": "30%"}
  ],
  "quota": {"per_minute": 1200, "consumption_estimate": "0.8"}
}
```

david: that looks fine. For enterprise, we should include a toggle \"show projected cost delta\" that uses last-30d token mix to estimate $ impact. but default off.

samir: implementation notes: evaluator needs access to routing policies, quota rules, and recent usage histograms. caching is crucial — compute for role+tenant and cache for 5m. invalidation on policy or model-catalog change.

alex: what about rollout UX — if admin pins a role to a model variant, preview should show that override and show fallbacks. also show telemetry flags (will we surface sampling/trace links)?

maya: product wants a \"why this route\" link expanding a short explanation and last-change info (who changed policy, when). that helps audits/compliance.

david: security: ensure the API respects scope scoping. service accounts used by console should only be allowed preview for tenants they manage. add an entitlement check in the preview endpoint.

samir: internal API debate: do we name it /entitlements/preview or /routing/simulate? the latter is more explicit but entitlements ties it to RBAC domain. lean /entitlements/preview to keep surface small.

alex: telemetry: we should emit a preview.event with fields {role_id, tenant_id, preview_mode, hash_of_policy} but NOT full policy. that will let us instrument adoption without leaking policy details.

david: ops note: preview could be used to probe capacity. rate-limit previews per tenant (e.g., 10/min) and per role. infra-bot should enforce.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: note — rate-limit middleware added to feature branch routing-preview.automations.

maya: next steps: samir + david to prototype endpoint + data-mapping, alex to mock console panel, i'll sync with product for copy and default toggles.

alex: thanks — ping me if you need constraints list for admin copy.

samir: i'll start an RFC draft for the preview evaluator and include perf/backoff semantics. will drop link here when ready.

david: I'll add the security checklist: scope checks, masking rules, and telemetry schema.

alex: perfect. Can we target a canary behind a flag in 2 weeks?

maya: 2 weeks sounds tight but doable for a minimal read-only preview. +1 on flagging behind enterprise feature gate.

samir: noted. planning to reuse existing caching layer; should hit the 2-week target for basic.

alex: ok closing. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
